name: Surena IV
maker: University of Tehran, Center of Advanced Systems and Technologies
def: Iranian full size humanoid with 43 degrees of freedom built to a low cost design that replaces force sensors with predictive foot contact sensing.
body: Surena IV stands 170 cm tall and weighs 68 kg, with seven degree of freedom arms, six degree of freedom hands, six degree of freedom legs, a two joint waist and a three joint neck driven by brushless motors through harmonic drives. Instead of costly six axis foot sensors it uses encoders at the foot corners to predict ground contact about 1.5 cm before touchdown, which lets it walk over unknown ground with small steps and slopes. The University of Tehran team unveiled it in December 2019 and has demonstrated grasping objects of varying stiffness, visual object tracking, writing and using a drill.
facts: Fourth generation of the Iranian Surena programme, which began in 2008
Uses low cost predictive foot sensors in place of six axis force sensors
The IEEE included it among the world's notable robots after assessing its performance
specs: Brushless direct current motors with harmonic drive gears
Predictive foot contact encoders, cameras, inertial unit
Onboard walking control with vision based manipulation
